name: Harold Pike
life: “I still remember opening the harbor gate at five winters' dawn.” Sunday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Harold takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I used to tell time from harbor smells. I took the new hire along on my early round.
appearance: Harold has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for soft white hair brushed sideways. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a moss-green cardigan with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Harold holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Harold gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Harold privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To teach the new hire the harbor's morning sounds.
family: Olivia Nielsen is Harold’s younger cousin. Harold brings a spare shopping bag. Olivia chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The worker who couldn't read the joke*, Olivia says, “I translated it too gently the first time. My friend deserves to know which actual word upset everybody.”
connections: Frances Ortiz. The keeper of harbor sounds helps confirm the repaired dial follows water again.

reactions.situation: A supervisor blames the new hire for missing the time
reactions.response: Harold checks which dial the worker saw before accepting a lateness entry.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Harold moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.situation: If a colleague lies to save face
reactions.response: Harold offers one private chance to correct it before the next conversation.
